messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER — elevated per-model TPM on asteria-13b in us-west-2. 95th latency > 2.5s, error rate rising. Auto-sculpt kicked in for other families. Paging oncall.
alex (oncall): saw it. opening thread. what's current surface-level customer impact?
elena (cust-ops): getting alerts from two large tenants (acme-inc, zephyr-ai) — their inference jobs showing 5xx and timeouts, reported via support. I'll queue them for notification if we escalate.
rita (eng-ops): metrics: asteria-13b TPM spiked from 1200 -> 3200 over last 12m, RPM similarly high. Queue depth on serving nodes up, KV cache miss rate up 40%.
nick (infra): some dedicated pools for asteria saturated. Autoscale attempted but hit GPU reservation caps for that fleet.
sre-maya: latency correlated with long-context requests ( > 8k tokens ). We saw many small streaming connections but large token counts; streaming retransmits piling up.
jordan (pm): any sign it's a client-side loop? or genuine traffic surge?
alex (oncall): sample of incoming prompts looks organic — batch generator jobs from a few keys (key-ACME-*) and some high-rate demo traffic. not obviously malicious.
rita (eng-ops): mitigation plan options:
- selective RPM cap reduce for asteria-13b
- apply per-key throttles for offending API keys
- temporarily disable streaming on asteria to reduce connection churn
- fallback routing to a lower-cost sibling model (asteria-7b-quant) for non-critical requests
alex (oncall): prefer targeted per-model RPM sculpt + disable streaming for long-context until stable. minimize customer-facing failures.
elena (cust-ops): if we switch customers to fallback model, should notify them. acme-inc is on a contract, ping account team?
jordan (pm): yes, ping AM. But first: reduce immediate pressure.
rita (eng-ops): suggested values: asteria-13b rpm -> 250, tpm -> 700 (soft); streaming disabled for requests > 4k tokens. Also set temporary per-key throttle for key-ACME-* to 100 rpm.
alex (oncall): I can make the RPM/TMP changes via the admin CLI and flip streaming flag. who will do per-key throttles?
nick (infra): I can apply per-key throttle via the rate limit service. prepping command.
alex (oncall): executing now.
alex (oncall): runbook action — quota change command:

```
# increase/decrease per-model runtime limits
ri-admin quota update --model asteria-13b --rpm 250 --tpm 700 --reason "live sculpting 2901234567"
ri-admin config set --model asteria-13b --streaming-max-tokens 4000 --reason "disable long streaming during surge"
```
alex (oncall): sent. (reacts :hammer_and_wrench:)
nick (infra): applying per-key throttle:
```
ratelimitctl set key key-ACME-* --rpm 100 --window 60s --owner "eng-oncall"
```
nick (infra): applied. confirming distributed config rollout.
sre-maya: seeing drop in queue depth already, 2m post-change. 95th latency dropping to ~1.6s.
rita (eng-ops): KV cache hit rate climbing back. error rate for acme down from 8% -> 2.1% within 3m.
elena (cust-ops): acme support ticket updated with mitigation steps and expected restoration window. AM looped in.
jordan (pm): flagging fallback routing as next step if numbers don't stabilize in 15m.
alex (oncall): action items logged. keeping streaming disabled for 30m then reassess. setting monitor:
- watch: asteria-13b:95p latency, error rate, queue depth
- alert if error rate > 5% or 95p latency > 2s
alex (oncall): creating incident note in linear: IN-7392 live sculpt asteria-13b (will attach logs)
rita (eng-ops): also enabling temporary increased logging for serving nodes to capture long-request traces (verbose=info)
nick (infra): config rollout completed across us-west-2 and fallback AZs.
sre-maya: traffic leveling looks stable; RPM now ~300 sustained vs 3200 spike before. tpm at ~680.
elena (cust-ops): acme reports their jobs are back to normal. zephyr-ai still seeing a few timeouts, possibly queueing in their end. I'll coordinate.
jordan (pm): good work. timeline: initial mitigation at ts=2901234580, observed improvement ts=2901234610.
alex (oncall): plan for next 60m: keep sculpt, monitor, hold on routing fallback. if error rate stays <3% for 30m, start gradual streaming re-enable for <=2k token reqs.
rita (eng-ops): agree. leaving a temporary hold on any deploys for models in us-west-2 until follow-up.
alex (oncall): postmortem owner? volunteer: rita.
rita (eng-ops): will own. will collect metrics, identify root cause (client spike vs autoscale shortfall), propose safeguards (auto per-key throttles earlier, preemptive fallback policy).
alex (oncall): wrap-up: actions taken listed in incident ticket, customers notified, oncall handing to day-shift at 2901234660. anyone else?
elena (cust-ops): will follow up with success emails to impacted tenants and note mitigation details.
alex (oncall): handover to day-shift. leaving thread open for 1h. thanks team :thumbsup:
